Kento Alpha 0.1, build 657

In this build

  • Playback runs at the comp's frame rate (it played as fast as frames came), and the playback menu's Speed works: a quarter, half, normal or twice the rate.
  • Motion: amplitude and frequency over time are curves you key in the window (click to key, drag, right-click to delete, or Draw), with the board's preset shapes and a linked frequency's response. A live motion shows as a chip on its curve and as a wave beside its knob: click either for Settings..., Switch off, Bake into keys or Remove motion. A reopened comp, in Kento or Nuke, keeps the motion.
  • Eases: Elastic and Bounce work (a key a frame between the two keys); Back's picture shows its overshoot.
  • Curve Editor: Scale X and Scale Y in the key bar (drag in the view to scale the selected keys in time or value), beside Scale and offset by numbers. The ruler and playhead no longer disappear with several keys selected. A right-click opens one menu, not two.
  • The Timeline shows the selected nodes' keys.
  • Text2: Nuke's text node, with its font, size, justification, colour, transform and shadow.
  • The expression helper's Wiggle and Oscillate open in Motion with their numbers (More in Motion...).
  • Every save writes Kento's own file, including the save on closing a window.
  • The Kento menu no longer repeats its items with several windows open.

The first build for compositors to try. It opens and saves Nuke-compatible scripts, and is meant for

new work as well as for playing old comps back.

Comps

  • Opens .nk scripts: all 1,388 scripts in Autonomy's census open, with 99% of their nodes built. Saves Nuke-compatible .nk, and .ko, Kento's own file, which keeps everything (tracks, solves, Kento's own settings).
  • Expressions on knobs, Nuke-compatible: worked out live where Kento can, and kept in the script where it can't yet. Known safe Python from comps runs.
  • Autosave, and recovery of an autosave newer than the comp.

Nodes

  • Nuke-compatible nodes, by the names compositors know and checked pixel for pixel: merges, grades, transforms (concatenating), blurs, keyers, Roto and RotoPaint, Read and Write (EXR, DPX, PNG, TIFF, JPEG, ProRes, H.264), 3D cards, cameras and ScanlineRender, and more.
  • New nodes start from your recent or most common values, or their defaults.

The Viewer

  • Up to four Viewers; compare and wipe; guides, aspect masks, rulers; the data passes (depth, motion, normals, IDs, position); Cryptomatte picking; pixel info.
  • On-screen controls for transforms, corner pins, crops, ramps, flares, the Tracker and the Sampler.

Roto and paint

  • Draw Bezier, B-spline, rectangle and ellipse shapes; edit points and tangents, key them (auto-key), set colour, feather and opacity.
  • Paint with a brush, eraser, clone or reveal, with pen pressure; a clone's source moved, turned and scaled. Edit painted strokes afterwards in the Layers panel: their lifetime, opacity, brush, colour and clone source; several at once.
  • The Layers panel: layers, shapes and strokes, renamed, duplicated and reordered by dragging.

Tracking

  • The Tracker tracks in Kento, with tolerance, hand-over to another feature keeping the offset, rejoining the original, and filling gaps from other tracks. Forward and back, or multipass.
  • Tracks over time: a lane per track. Exports to Transform and CornerPin2D, linked or baked.

Expressions

  • The expression helper (Utility menu): Link, Choose, Offset in time, Hold, Wiggle, Oscillate, Ramp, Step, Loop, Clamp and Size, with a live curve; pixel recipes for keys and masks.
  • The pick-whip: drag a knob's state mark onto another knob to link it, or onto a node in the Node Graph to choose one of its knobs.

Help

  • Report a problem: what happened, the comp, the log and the Mac's details, saved as a .zip and filed in the studio bug tracker.

Not yet

  • Proxy and downscale, and the manual: in the menus, dim.
  • Paint's blur, sharpen, smear, dodge and burn; a clone source from another frame.
  • Roto open splines.

Kento Alpha 0.1, build 640

In this build

  • Backdrops: grab one anywhere to move it, and resize it from a wide band at any edge or corner. Its settings show in Properties when you click it, and the graph updates as you change them. Double-click its title or its note to edit them on the graph; the note's box grows with its lines.
  • Flipbook (Viewer > Flipbook..., Alt+F): renders in the background to the cache, playing in the Viewer as the Timeline fills green, or to a QuickTime in its own player that you can save. It can leave a cache node (DiskCache) after the node you flipbooked.
  • Open and save in Kento's own dialog: favourites (the comp's folder, its shot and show, Renders, folders you star), recent folders, filters for comps, footage, this shot's versions and this week, a preview of what a comp holds, Version up.
  • Motion (the Curve Editor's Motion button, or a knob's menu): shakes, noise, waves and eases as cards with their waveforms. Bake one into keys, or add it on top, live: the knob's keys stay keyable underneath and the motion's settings become knobs you can key too. Nuke opens it the same.
  • Expressions read Nuke's curve (a knob's own keys).
  • Properties: several selected nodes get a panel of their own (group, Bento, backdrop, note, align, move by, colour, lock, disable, shared values); closed sections list what's changed in them; saturation's slider in greys; a Dot's panel.
  • Problems in plain words where they happen: a card when you rest on a red node, with fixes (Relink..., Show in Finder, nearest frame); the same at the top of the node's Properties; the Viewer names what it shows in place of a missing frame; a failed render shows a card with Retry from the frame that failed; an amber dot on a node that works but needs a look.
  • Curve Editor: box zoom (Control+Option and drag), Key properties (Enter), copy and paste whole curves, auto-clamped tangents, lane bars in the Ghost.
  • Dope Sheet: chevrons to fold a node's rows, the node's colour by its name, Ghost (curves behind the keys), Footage only.
  • Node Graph: jump labels (a long wire as two named tags), dotted lines for linked values, Select What Reads It, a group in its own tab (Cmd+Return), O for Roto, P for RotoPaint, Shift and a letter to branch, Shift+A for AddMix, Alt+N for a sticky note. Shift-snapping no longer lands nodes off the grid.
  • Scopes, from the Viewer bar's chart button.
  • Write: numbers its files by an offset, a start frame or an expression, and Render all follows each Write's render order.
  • The interface's brightness lifts every grey together.
  • numpy is part of Kento.

Kento Alpha 0.1, build 594

In this build

  • The Curve Editor shows its curves and keys again, and frames them when a node is selected.
  • The Curve Editor in its design: the key bar and view row, curves and keys in their channels' colours, the curve list with its eyes, and a dope strip under the curves.
  • Scale keys with the selection's box: its corners scale time and value, its sides time, its top and bottom value. Scale and offset by numbers, nudge with the arrow keys, flip, reverse, smooth, normalise, simplify, and an Euler filter for rotations.
  • Ease keys from the Ease grid; break tangents; copy, paste and delete keys; set a curve's before and after (cycle, cycle with offset, oscillate, linear).
  • Backdrops: a title bar to grab them, sticky (their nodes move with them) or a patch, resized from any corner or edge, and their own panel: colour, opacity, title size, a title that stays readable zoomed out.
  • Backdrops from .nk scripts keep their size.
  • Zoomed out, a node's ports appear as the pointer comes near; dragging a wire shows every input it could go to, and dropping it on a node connects the nearest.
  • The Node Graph zooms in four times closer.
  • Every popup can be moved out of the way, and opens again where it was left.
  • Updates show their progress as they download.
  • Tooltips at the size of the rest of the interface.
